meta.note: Every parameter below carries a source and a plausible range. The chain that consumes them lives in src/lib/cascade.js. Where a figure is derived from first principles rather than cited, the derivation is written out in full.

assumptions.label: Model class
assumptions.help: Energy per output token varies by two orders of magnitude across model classes. This is the single largest source of uncertainty in the whole chain.

options.label: Mid-size
options.note: the efficient end of production serving

assumptions.label: Accelerator service life
assumptions.help: Microsoft, Google and CoreWeave depreciate over six years; Meta over five and a half. Critics argue the real economic life is closer to three.

options.label: 3 years
options.note: the bear case — obsolescence, not failure

assumptions.label: Fleet utilisation
assumptions.help: The fraction of its life the part spends doing useful work. Amortised capital cost, water and embodied energy all scale inversely with this.

assumptions.label: Grid carbon intensity
assumptions.help: Where the electrons come from. This changes the emissions answer by two orders of magnitude and nothing else in the chain.

options.label: 700 — coal-heavy
options.note: parts of Asia and the US Midwest

overheadMultiplier.label: Host, idle and datacentre overhead
overheadMultiplier.derivation: Google reports 0.24 Wh per median Gemini text prompt on a comprehensive basis versus 0.10 Wh counting active accelerators only — a 2.4× multiplier. The breakdown is 58% accelerator, 25% host CPU and memory, 10% idle capacity, 8% datacentre overhead.

source.what: Measuring the environmental impact of AI inference

acceleratorPowerW.label: Accelerator board power
acceleratorPowerW.derivation: H100 SXM is 700 W; Blackwell-class parts run at roughly 1 kW and above. Used to convert energy back into occupancy time.

waferEqPerGpu.label: Wafer-equivalents per accelerator
waferEqPerGpu.derivation: A Blackwell-class part is two reticle-limited logic dies (~1,600 mm²), eight HBM stacks (~6,000 mm² of DRAM across 64 thinned dies), and a CoWoS interposer spanning more than three reticles (~3,000 mm²) — roughly 10,600 mm² of silicon in total against a 70,686 mm² wafer, before yield and edge exclusion. Most of the silicon in an AI accelerator is memory, not compute.

source.what: Blackwell: 208 bn transistors across two reticle-limited dies

waferMassG.label: Mass of one 300 mm wafer
waferMassG.derivation: π × (150 mm)² = 70,686 mm² = 706.9 cm². At 775 µm thickness that is 54.8 cm³, and silicon is 2.329 g/cm³ — so 127.6 g. Derived, not cited.

polyPerWafer.label: Polysilicon consumed per finished wafer
polyPerWafer.derivation: Slicing loses kerf: an as-cut wafer of ~850 µm plus ~130 µm of diamond-wire kerf means 980 µm of ingot per 775 µm of finished wafer, a 1.26× penalty. Ingot crop, grinding and test slices take roughly a further 18%. 127.6 g × 1.26 ÷ 0.82 ≈ 197 g.

source.what: kerf 60–150 µm for fixed-diamond wire; crop yield assumed

quartzitePerWafer.label: Quartzite feedstock per wafer
quartzitePerWafer.derivation: SiO₂ → Si is a 60.08 : 28.09 mass ratio, so 2.14 g of silica per gram of silicon at best. Carbothermic reduction runs ~87% and the Siemens route ~85% on silicon utilisation. 197 g × 2.14 ÷ (0.87 × 0.85) ≈ 569 g. This is ordinary quartzite for the smelter — not the high-purity quartz below.

cruciblePerWafer.label: High-purity crucible quartz per wafer
cruciblePerWafer.derivation: A Czochralski crucible is a consumable — one per pull. Assuming ~15 kg of fused quartz per crucible and a ~200 kg ingot yielding ~1,000 wafers of polysilicon-equivalent, that is ~15 g per wafer. This is the material that comes from Spruce Pine.

source.what: crucible mass and ingot yield assumed

fabWaterPerWafer.label: Ultra-pure water per wafer start
fabWaterPerWafer.derivation: Advanced fabs consume 4.5–7 L of UPW per cm² of processed wafer; the 2021 industry average was 8.22 L/cm². Across 706.9 cm² that is 3,180–5,810 L per 300 mm wafer.

source.what: Environmental data and facts in semiconductor manufacturing

fabEnergyPerWafer.label: Fab electricity per wafer start
fabEnergyPerWafer.derivation: Industry average 1.15 kWh/cm² in 2021 × 706.9 cm² ≈ 812 kWh per 300 mm wafer, covering the full 1,000–1,500 step flow over three to four months.

source.what: Environmental data and facts in semiconductor manufacturing

coolingWaterPerWh.label: Datacentre cooling water
coolingWaterPerWh.derivation: Google reports 0.26 mL of water alongside 0.24 Wh for the median Gemini text prompt — 1.083 mL per Wh. Highly site-dependent: evaporative cooling trades water for electricity, closed-loop designs do the reverse.

source.what: Measuring the environmental impact of AI inference

tokenEnergyRange.label: Energy per output token
tokenEnergyRange.derivation: Epoch AI places inference at roughly 1×10⁻⁴ to 2×10⁻³ Wh per output token depending on model size, with GPT-4o-class serving near 3×10⁻⁴. Extended-reasoning models generating long chains of thought reach ~3.3×10⁻² Wh per prompt-token-equivalent — two orders of magnitude higher.

source.what: How much energy does ChatGPT use?
